deposits.notes:
Original Lee and Chung (2024) data used by the c015 reanalysis; S1=Exp1, S2=Exp2A, S3=Exp2B, S4=Exp3, S5=Exp4, S6=Exp5. Public node and anonymous file downloads confirmed. Both web URLs also occur in the screening form, but found_by='paper' takes precedence. There are 47 files, all listed here, and zero child nodes. Root, every experiment folder, Robustness_Experts folder and children endpoint returned HTTP 200. OSF node_license is null and no license file was listed.

rows_checked and columns_checked refer specifically to Exp5/Exp5.main.qualtrics.csv (HTTP 200, 582955 bytes): 575 raw survey rows with distinct ResponseId values, including incomplete/excluded responses. Condition, Empathy and idea columns are present; raw row counts are not analyzed sample sizes. Other raw main files were also read: Exp1/Exp1.main.qualtrics.csv: 1118 raw survey rows; Exp2A/Exp2A.main.qualtrics.csv: 428 raw survey rows; Exp2B/Exp2B.main.qualtrics.csv: 356 raw survey rows; Exp3/Exp3.main.qualtrics.csv: 575 raw survey rows; Exp4/Exp4.main.qualtrics.csv: 547 raw survey rows; Exp5/Exp5.main.qualtrics.csv: 575 raw survey rows. Exp1.main.qualtrics.handcoded.csv has 263 rows and supplies idea_1 through idea_20, idea_count_jc and idea_text_raw.

All six main Qualtrics rating CSVs were read in memory. Exp1/Exp1.rating.qualtrics.csv: 513 rater rows, 2437 columns; Exp2A/Exp2A.rating.qualtrics.csv: 316 rater rows, 1786 columns; Exp2B/Exp2B.rating.qualtrics.csv: 349 rater rows, 1852 columns; Exp3/Exp3.rating.qualtrics.csv: 217 rater rows, 2204 columns; Exp4/Exp4.rating.qualtrics.csv: 396 rater rows, 2470 columns; Exp5/Exp5.rating.qualtrics.csv: 388 rater rows, 2387 columns. Ratings are wide, with columns such as 1_creative_1, 1_creative_2, 1_creative_3, 1_practical_1, 1_practical_2, 1_practical_3. Experiment 5 includes a factor suffix, e.g. 1_creative_H_1 and 1_practical_H_1. These rows are evaluators, not randomized idea-generators, and must be reshaped and joined through the idea crosswalks.

All idea-to-participant crosswalks were read. They contain Unnamed: 0 (the exported row index), ResponseId, workerId, idea_text and idea_text_id. Exp1/Exp1.rating.link.csv: 400 rows, 236 distinct ResponseId; Exp2A/Exp2A.rating.link.csv: 291 rows, 291 distinct ResponseId; Exp2B/Exp2B.rating.link.csv: 300 rows, 300 distinct ResponseId; Exp3/Exp3.rating.link.csv: 197 rows, 197 distinct ResponseId; Exp4/Exp4.rating.link.csv: 405 rows, 405 distinct ResponseId; Exp5/Exp5.rating.link_Baseline.csv: 197 rows, 197 distinct ResponseId; Exp5/Exp5.rating.link_EmpathyHigh.csv: 194 rows, 194 distinct ResponseId. Use the experiment-specific Rmd join rules: some studies use the exported row index, whereas Experiment 1 uses idea_text_id. Do not assume every crosswalk's row count is an analyzed participant count.

Expert outcome files were also read: Robustness_Experts/Exp4.rating.experts.csv: 405 idea rows; Robustness_Experts/Exp1.rating.experts.csv: 400 idea rows; Robustness_Experts/Exp2A.rating.experts.csv: 291 idea rows; Robustness_Experts/Exp2B.rating.experts.csv: 300 idea rows; Robustness_Experts/Exp3.rating.experts.csv: 197 idea rows; Robustness_Experts/Exp5.rating.experts_Baseline.csv: 197 idea rows; Robustness_Experts/Exp5.rating.experts_High.csv: 194 idea rows. Their idea_id keys and Novelty_ha/ya/ak and Practicality_ha/ya/ak columns are observed; several files additionally contain Verbosity and Articulate ratings. Exp1/Exp1.analyze.Rmd, Exp2A/Exp2A.analyze.Rmd and Exp5/Exp5.analyze.Rmd were downloaded and read. They specify evaluator filtering, six rating dimensions, ORIGINALITY, APPROPRIATENESS and OVERALL composites, and averaging over each participant's ideas before the participant-level analysis. Main files contain arm assignment; crosswalks link idea IDs and texts to participant ResponseId; rater files supply outcome scores.

Reconstruct retained samples using the posted cleaning scripts or the companion cleaned data in zf3s2. In particular, Experiment 1 can have several rated ideas per participant, and Experiment 2b adds 100 AI-only outputs. The Exp5 Rmd refers to Exp5.rating.link_High.csv, while the public filename is Exp5.rating.link_EmpathyHigh.csv; adapt that local filename rather than treating the crosswalk as absent. Some initial download/API calls timed out; successful retries are the basis of this classification. No analysis scripts were executed and no downloaded data were saved to disk.

Public original-study datasets copied into the reanalysis project, plus the analysis notebook and separate arm-specific idea pools; this is not a code-only deposit. The OSF landing page, node metadata, storage listing, all six experiment-folder listings, and children endpoint returned HTTP 200. There are 27 files and zero child nodes; inventory includes all files. OSF node_license is null and no license file was listed.

rows_checked and columns_checked refer specifically to exp_2a/Exp2A.main.full.csv, downloaded and parsed in memory (HTTP 200, 533659 bytes). It has 291 distinct, nonempty ResponseId values and complete ORIGINALITY, APPROPRIATENESS, OVERALL, Original, Innovative, Creative, Practical, Effective and Useful scores. Read with keep_default_na=False: Condition is the literal string 'None' for 95 human-only participants, 'Google' for 100 and 'Chatbot' for 96. Default pandas NA parsing mistakenly converts 'None' into a missing value. All 95 human_ideas.csv entries match the Condition='None' participants' idea entries after whitespace normalization.

Other main files downloaded and parsed (all HTTP 200): exp_1/Exp1.main.cleaned.csv has 233 unique ResponseId rows (Control=130, Chatbot=103); exp_2b/Exp2B.main.cleaned.csv has 300 unique ResponseId rows (HumanOnly=98, ChatbotHuman=102, ChatbotOnly=100); exp_3/Exp3.main.cleaned.csv has 194 unique ResponseId rows (Google=99, Chatbot=95); exp_4/Exp4.main.cleaned.csv and exp_4/Exp4.main.joined.csv each have 400 unique ResponseId rows (Google=202, Chatbot=198); exp_5/Exp5.main.cleaned.csv has 383 unique ResponseId rows. The 100 ChatbotOnly rows are AI outputs, not human participants; thus Experiment 2b has 200 human participants in these files. Study mapping: exp_1=S1, exp_2a=S2, exp_2b=S3, exp_3=S4, exp_4=S5, exp_5=S6.

Experiment 4's joined file has the same nine complete rating columns as Experiment 2a, plus Condition and NumCon. Other cleaned files retain participant IDs, arm labels and idea texts but do not contain these joined creativity-rating columns; obtain their ratings through rzn87. Experiment 5 has Condition and Empathy: Chatbot/Baseline=105, Chatbot/High=108, Google/Baseline=89, Google/High=81. Each cell count was also confirmed by reading the corresponding one-column idea CSV with header=None. These are analyzed sample counts, not recruitment or randomized counts.

Experiment 1's headerless chatbot_ideas.csv has 103 text rows, all exactly matching the 103 Chatbot participants' idea_text_raw values after stripping surrounding whitespace; 37 of those participants have idea_count_jc > 1. The control pool has 130 rows, of which 128 exactly match Control idea_text_raw values; 44 Control participants have idea_count_jc > 1, and the two remaining text differences were not resolved by collapsing whitespace. The notebook reads each whole CSV field, strips whitespace and embeds it without splitting ideas. Whole participant submissions containing several ideas therefore enter the diversity analysis; two control-text discrepancies remain for a replication audit. The pool CSVs themselves have no headers or participant-ID columns, but the companion main files supply participant IDs and arm assignment.

analysis.ipynb was downloaded (HTTP 200, 36791 bytes) and read without execution. It specifies https://tfhub.dev/google/universal-sentence-encoder/4, unique fractions, centroid similarity, average pairwise similarity and minimum-spanning-tree distances. It uses Bonferroni-adjusted alpha=0.05/n_comparisons for proportion-difference Wald CIs and Bonferroni-multiplied p-values from pooled two-proportion z-tests. Different CI/test standard errors can explain an adjusted p-value above .05 alongside a CI excluding zero; no claim is made that every other metric's printed interval is corrected. No embeddings, per-idea similarity-score export or executed results file was listed. Diversity scores must be regenerated from the available text and code.

Supplementary Table 1 (PDF SI p. 5, Study 3) prints web-search n=95 and GPT-aided n=99; the downloaded exp_3 main file labels Google=99 and Chatbot=95. Preserve this discrepancy for the later numerical audit rather than silently changing either source.

deposits.notes: The exact supplementary-file URL is in forms/c015.json source.supplement; the paper points to its DOI landing page. All eight supplementary PDF pages were read in memory. Supplementary Table 1 (SI pp. 2-8) provides aggregate condition values, counts (except Experiment 5 cells), effect sizes and inferential statistics; it has no participant records or participant texts. has_outcome_scores=true refers to aggregate scores only; has_arm_assignment=false means no participant-to-arm map. The publisher landing page https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-025-02173-x and DOI both returned HTTP 200 with a 'Client Challenge' page, so no complete supplementary-file inventory could be obtained there. n_files=1 counts this verified file, not an assertion about the publisher's entire inventory. The known direct supplement URL loaded without credentials. The reporting summary is already included in the local 10-page article PDF. No further data/code/materials availability statement was present in the supplementary PDF.

Related deposit returned by the OSF title-filter search for 'Meincke', titled 'Reply to Meincke et al.'; it is not confirmed to cover any of c015's S1-S6 and is not used to establish availability for those studies. Public landing page, node metadata, storage root, Study folder and children endpoint returned HTTP 200; five files and no child nodes. CR6_dataset.csv was read (HTTP 200, 55138 bytes): 109 raw rows; all Condition values are blank. The own column contains free-text definitions of a creative idea, and dv has 101 numeric binary values (0/1). StartDate values fall on 20 December 2024. CR6_analyze.Rmd (HTTP 200, 1422 bytes, read without execution) filters participant IDs and attention checks, then runs a one-sample proportion test on dv against .50. This is an ancillary survey about creativity judgments, not evidence of the original randomized ChatGPT-versus-control samples. The text and binary outcome flags refer only to this ancillary survey. OSF node_license is null; no license file was listed.

what_we_could_compute: final.open_items: Experiment 5 per-cell analyzed counts. Direct counts in exp_5/Exp5.main.cleaned.csv and the four arm-specific idea CSVs are ChatGPT/base empathy=105, ChatGPT/high empathy=108, web search/base empathy=89, web search/high empathy=81 (total 383).

final.open_items: per-condition analyzed counts, comparison statistics and intervals. The original participant/text/rating files and the reanalysis notebook allow reconstruction for S1-S6, with the 100 AI-only Experiment 2b outputs excluded from human sample counts. Supplementary Table 1 already supplies many aggregate results, but the data enable verification and alternative contrasts.

final.open_items: how Experiment 1 entries containing several ideas were embedded. The notebook embeds one complete CSV field per row. All 103 Chatbot pool texts match participant idea_text_raw values, including 37 participants with multiple handcoded ideas. Of 130 control texts, 128 match exactly; two require further reconciliation. The data and code establish that multi-idea participant entries were not generally split into separate embeddings.

final.open_items: confidence-interval correction audit. The public notebook explicitly applies Bonferroni-adjusted alpha to unique-fraction difference CIs and multiplicity correction to pooled two-proportion z-test p-values; these can be recomputed and compared against Supplementary Table 1. This does not by itself verify every printed CI for the alternative diversity measures.

The public data also support participant-level mean creativity/originality/appropriateness scores and per-arm means, sample SDs, SEs and analyzed counts after the posted exclusions and participant-to-idea/rater joins. Experiment 2a and Experiment 4 have these participant scores already joined in zf3s2; rzn87 supplies outcome ratings and crosswalks for all six experiments.

The participant-linked texts and analysis.ipynb permit recomputing unique-concept fractions at thresholds .75/.80/.85, centroid and mean pairwise cosine similarities, and minimum-spanning-tree diversity. Per-participant summaries and participant-resampling uncertainty can be constructed where appropriate. The primary unique-concept fraction is a set-level statistic, so its uncertainty is not an ordinary SD/SE over independent idea pairs.
notes:
Entire local markdown conversion read in chunks: 462 lines, including the 3-page article and all 7 pages of the Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary. Data/code/materials passages were checked against the local PDF text with pymupdf (especially PDF pp. 3-5). The separate 8-page supplementary PDF was downloaded into memory and fully read. Quotations retain the markdown's bracketed superscript reference markers; typographic bold/italic delimiters are removed. Unfilled generic reporting-template prompts (e.g. genomics/clinical data) are not study-specific availability claims. No preregistration URL was stated in this paper.

Classification is based on downloaded and parsed participant-level CSVs, not just the authors' availability statement or the HTTP 200 OSF application shell. The original rzn87 data and the reanalysis zf3s2 files jointly cover S1-S6. The related 835bg reply survey is included for completeness of the search audit but is not counted as evidence for any of those studies. The supplementary PDF is aggregate only.

Confidence is high for public data availability. Exact replication still requires the posted cleaning/join rules, separation of AI-only outputs, regeneration of diversity scores, reconciliation of two Experiment 1 control texts, and examination of the Experiment 3 arm-count reversal between data labels and Supplementary Table 1. The ancillary reply study and publisher bot challenge do not undermine direct access to the two verified data repositories. A materials-correspondence address is not treated as an on-request restriction on these public data.

Requests used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifier. No login, account creation, access request, CAPTCHA solution, or bot-check bypass was attempted. All remote CSVs, code and PDFs inspected were under 20 MB and held only in memory. No analysis code from deposits was executed. The only file written is forms/data/c015.json.
